chunks: ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام about an Imam who invalidated his wudu (ablution), withdrew, and did not appoint anyone: what is the condition of the people? He said:
"There is no salat (prayer) for them except with an Imam, so let some of them put one of themselves forward, and let him complete with them what remains of it, and their prayer has been completed."

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: invalidated his state of ritual purity, such as by breaking wudu (ablution)
key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader of the congregation
key_terms.الْقَوْمِ: the congregation or group praying behind the Imam
key_terms.انْصَرَفَ: withdrew or left the prayer place
key_terms.بِإِمَامٍ: with a prayer leader in congregational worship
key_terms.تَمَّتْ صَلَاتُهُمْ: their prayer is complete and valid
key_terms.يُقَدِّمْ: appoint or put someone forward to lead

ai.seo_question: What should a congregation do if the Imam breaks wudu (ablution) and leaves during salat (prayer) without appointing a replacement?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for congregational salat (prayer) when the Imam invalidates his wudu (ablution) and leaves without appointing a replacement. One of the congregation should step forward to lead the remainder, and the congregational prayer remains valid and completed for them.
